haiku-low.q1: One run is created for the most recent missed fire time, and it is claimed by the first idle worker. The two earlier missed fire times get no rows and are dropped.
haiku-low.q2: A run for the new fire time is recorded with status skipped and finished_at set to now. It is not executed.
haiku-low.q3: Three tries in total. The wait is 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2. After the third failure the run is marked failed with final_error.
haiku-low.q4: After its heartbeat is more than 2 minutes old, a sweep closes the attempt as presumed_dead and the run is retried after the wait. Yes, that attempt counts toward the 3 used.
haiku-low.q5: Queued runs, including those waiting to retry, are cancelled. A running run finishes, but if it fails with retries left it is cancelled, not requeued. Fire times during the pause create no runs, and on resume missed ones are not caught up.
haiku-low.q6: The row lock from FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the due schedule lets only one worker create runs. A duplicate insert on (schedule_id, fire_time) does nothing as a safety net.
haiku-low.q7: It is kept in JOB_SCHEDULES.next_fire_at as a UTC time. It is set on save, enable and tenant resume, and moved to the next occurrence after now when a run is created.
haiku-low.q8: One statement picks a due queued run with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and, in the same statement, sets it running, adds 1 to attempt_count, and sets claimed_by. Locked rows are skipped, so no two workers take the same run.
haiku-low.q9: It is kept in JOB_RUNS.heartbeat_at, refreshed every 30 seconds by the running worker. The 30-second sweep by any worker finds running runs whose heartbeat is over 2 minutes old.
haiku-low.q10: The wait is stored as next_attempt_at on the queued JOB_RUNS row, set to now plus 1 or 5 minutes. A claim picks it up once next_attempt_at is at or before now.
haiku-low.q11: Once per fire time: one JOB_RUNS row, unique on (schedule_id, fire_time). Once per execution try: one JOB_RUN_ATTEMPTS row, keyed by (run_id, attempt_no).
haiku-low.q12: Its outcome write is guarded by WHERE status='running' AND attempt_count = its own number. The newer claim has raised attempt_count, so the old write changes zero rows and writes nothing.

sonnet.q1: Only one run: for the latest missed fire time F (most recent occurrence at or before now). Earlier two missed fire times get no rows and are dropped. The run is created on the next 30-second tick (as queued, or skipped if another run is queued/running) and claimed by the first idle worker.
sonnet.q2: A run row for the new fire time is inserted with status 'skipped' and finished_at = now(), if the previous run is queued or running (including waiting to retry). It is not executed, and it shows in history.
sonnet.q3: At most 3 attempts. Wait is 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2 (run goes back to queued with next_attempt_at = now() + wait). After attempt 3 fails the run becomes 'failed' with final_error and finished_at set. (If the schedule is disabled/deleted or tenant paused, it is cancelled instead of requeued.)
sonnet.q4: After its heartbeat is more than 2 minutes stale, a 30-second sweep by any worker marks the attempt presumed_dead (error 'heartbeat timeout') and requeues the run with the wait (1 min after attempt 1, 5 min after attempt 2), so the retry can start up to about 2 minutes plus the wait after the crash. Yes, it uses up an attempt. If it was attempt 3, the run becomes failed with final_error 'heartbeat timeout'.
sonnet.q5: Pausing sets jobs_paused_at and cancels the queued run (status cancelled, finished_at set; earlier attempts stay, final_error empty). The running run is left alone and finishes normally; if it fails with retries left it is cancelled instead of requeued. During the pause, paused tenant's schedules are not selected, so no runs are created for fire times. On resume, jobs_paused_at is cleared and next_fire_at is set to the first occurrence after now for every enabled schedule; missed fire times are not caught up and cancelled runs are not revived.
sonnet.q6: Selection of due schedules uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so the row lock lets only one worker process a schedule; the other skips it. As a safety net, UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING ignores a duplicate insert. The same transaction also moves next_fire_at forward.
sonnet.q7: In JOB_SCHEDULES.next_fire_at (UTC, partial index WHERE enabled). It changes when a schedule is saved/created, enabled (set to first occurrence after now), on tenant resume (for every enabled schedule), and in the 30-second run-creation transaction (set to first occurrence after now). It stays old while a tenant is paused, and is unchanged if run creation rolls back.
sonnet.q8: One statement picks a due queued run (next_attempt_at <= now(), schedule enabled and not deleted, tenant not paused) with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and in the same statement sets status = running, increments attempt_count, sets claimed_by and heartbeat_at, and inserts the attempt row. Locked rows are skipped by other workers, and once committed the row is running and no longer matches.
sonnet.q9: In JOB_RUNS.heartbeat_at (set on claim, refreshed every 30 s by the running worker with a guarded UPDATE). It is noticed by the crash-recovery sweep that any worker runs every 30 seconds, which finds running runs with heartbeat_at older than 2 minutes by the database clock.
sonnet.q10: In JOB_RUNS.next_attempt_at, with status set back to queued (now() + 1 min or 5 min). The retry starts when a worker's 5-second claim tick, while idle, finds the queued run with next_attempt_at <= now() and claims it like any new run.
sonnet.q11: Once per fire time: one JOB_RUNS row (unique on schedule_id, fire_time), including skipped and cancelled ones. Once per execution try: one JOB_RUN_ATTEMPTS row (run_id, attempt_no), at most 3 per run.
sonnet.q12: Its outcome write is a guarded write (WHERE status = 'running' AND attempt_count = ?) using its old fencing token. Since the run's status or attempt_count has changed after takeover, the update changes zero rows and it writes nothing. If it races with the sweep, the first to commit wins and the second re-checks its WHERE and changes zero rows.
